Adventure movement modal: text-producing native control flow

Source images and exact function boundaries are in image-sources.json.
This is a disk-only decompilation of text production, not a rendering result.
The complete instructions, branches, operands and calls remain in the adjacent
ASM and TSV source artifacts. Native field names below are descriptive aliases;
unknown structures keep their offsets rather than invented type names.

Address convention
  The modal body in the two configured images has the same instruction layout.
  Every modal RVA below is reference RVA; classic RVA = reference RVA - 0x2780.
  reference body 0x874800..0x877111, tables 0x877114..0x877260.
  classic body   0x872080..0x874991, tables 0x874994..0x874AE0.
  unit-title helper: reference 0x132E430..0x132F971,
                     classic   0x13293A0..0x132A8E1 (difference 0x5090).
  shortcut helper: reference 0xC394B0..0xC395B5,
                   classic   0xC364F0..0xC365F5.
  shortcut-name: reference 0x8ECB30..0x8ECE32,
                 classic   0x8EA360..0x8EA662.

Modal data
  modal = incoming rcx (r13 until the lower factors section reuses registers).
  unit = *(modal + 0x10).
  gaitCategory = int32(modal + 0x18).
  viewportScroll = int32(modal + 0x04).
  unitRaw = *(unit + 0x5F8).
  gait vector begin = *(unitRaw + 0xE8 + 0x18 * gaitCategory).
  gait vector end   = *(unitRaw + 0xF0 + 0x18 * gaitCategory).
  selected gait index = int32(unit + 0xDE8 + 4 * gaitCategory).
  unit coordinates are int16(unit + 0xA8, +0xAA, +0xAC).
  prone bit = uint32(unit + 0x110) & 0x8000.

Top button and title
  0x874A18 -> "Done"; draw 0x874A37.
  0x874A68 -> title = "How will ".
  0x874A79 -> subject = "you".
  0x874A8D -> unit = *(modal + 0x10).
  0x874A91 -> compare unit with adventure-player pointer:
              reference global RVA 0x23E5110, classic global RVA 0x23DF000.
  0x874A98 -> if equal, skip subject production at 0x874AAF.
  0x874A9A..0x874AAF -> otherwise unit_title(unit, subject, 1, 0, 1).
  0x874ABF -> append the complete dynamic subject to title.
  0x874AC4..0x874ACF -> append " move?".
  0x874AE2 -> draw the entire assembled title in one string draw call.

  subject is not restricted to ASCII or to one noun. It may already contain a
  Chinese species/identity string when the outer grammar reaches translation.
  Preserve the dynamic middle's identity source and process both outer literals.

Gait list, all rows (0x874B1F..0x875BFB)
  row count is the selected category's vector length, not six.
  visible rows are limited by modal dimensions and viewportScroll.
  each visible row uses row_index - viewportScroll + 0x52 as its shortcut enum.
  0x874D82..0x874D8C -> draw_shortcut(shortcut enum).
  0x874DD7..0x874DE7 -> gait = vector[row_index], nameIndex = int32(gait + 0).
  0x874DEA..0x874E09 -> require nameIndex >= 0 and nameIndex < names.size().
  global name vector: reference begin/end RVAs 0x24ECAB8/0x24ECAC0;
                      classic begin/end RVAs 0x24E69A8/0x24E69B0.
  0x874E0B..0x874E2A -> copy the string from names[nameIndex].
  0x874E35..0x874E46 -> invalid index: name = "Move".
  0x874E4A..0x874ED8 -> constrain to available native row width.
    if original length reaches width threshold, resize to available width;
    when that width exceeds three, replace its last three bytes with "...".
  0x874EEA -> draw gait name.

  Thus native gait names are sourced from GAIT raw tokens/variation arguments,
  not a native switch over Walk, Run or the screenshot's six visible labels.
  raw-gait-sources.tsv retains every GAIT token per image/object/caste/variation.
  raw-gait-applications.tsv retains every *_GAITS application and arguments.

  0x874EF7..0x874F07 -> save selection; temporarily set selection = row_index.
  0x874F1B..0x874F2F -> if int16(unit + 0x4CC) == -30000 (0x8AD0),
                       go to normal speed production at 0x8754A6.
  otherwise climbing production:
    0x874F39..0x874F4F -> tint from uint32(unit + 0x110) & 0x40000.
    0x874F59..0x874F66 -> raw = movement_speed(unit, 0, 1, &flags).
                         reference helper RVA 0x1334C10,
                         classic helper RVA 0x132FB80.
    0x874F6B..0x874F76 -> value = 1000000 / (raw + 100).
    0x874F9B..0x874FC1 -> draw "Climb ".
    0x875025..0x875227 -> number text, including literal decimal ".", zero
                         padding and temporary remainder cleanup branches.
    0x875237 -> draw numeric string.
    0x87525D..0x875382 -> compare climbing target coordinates
                        unit+0x4CC/+0x4CE/+0x4D0 against unit position;
                        build directional bits, then planar and up/down glyphs.
  normal speed production:
    0x8754A6..0x8754C1 -> tint from uint32(unit + 0x110) & 0x40000.
    0x8754CB..0x8754D7 -> raw0 = movement_speed(unit, 0, 0, &flags).
    0x8754DC..0x8754E7 -> value0 = 1000000 / (raw0 + 100).
    0x8754E9..0x8754F5 -> raw1 = movement_speed(unit, 0, 1, &flags).
    0x8754FA..0x875505 -> value1 = 1000000 / (raw1 + 100).
    0x87551F..0x875550 -> draw "Speed: ".
    0x8755AF..0x8755B1 -> equal values: one decimal number.
    otherwise: value1 + "/" + value0 (separator load 0x8756F8).
    integer digits, "." and zero padding are numeric text branches; the
    separate direction/up/down glyphs are retained as glyphs.
    0x87586B -> draw numeric string.
  0x875455..0x875461 -> restore saved selected gait before advancing row.
  Selection affects frame/tint; it does not add a new text literal.

Exact numeric formatting and non-word glyph switches
  All divisions here use signed integer truncation toward zero.
  All numbers are produced from the helper result for the current temporary
  selected gait; neither translation nor row joining should reinterpret them.
  Common full numeric path for Climb and equal speed:
    q = value / 1000; output = decimal(q) + ".".
    remainderText = decimal(value - 1000*q).
    if remainderText.length <= 2, append one "0" to output.
    if remainderText.length == 1, append another "0" to output.
    append remainderText to output.
    Native code then trims the temporary remainder string while length >= 4
    and its last two bytes are both "0". The temporary was already appended
    by value, so this cleanup does not remove zeros from the displayed output.
  Climb path:
    quotient production 0x875025..0x87503E;
    dot 0x8750BE..0x8750C9;
    remainder production 0x8750F1..0x87511A;
    first zero decision 0x87515F..0x875173;
    second zero decision 0x87517C..0x875190;
    remainder append 0x875199..0x8751AB;
    temporary trim length gate 0x8751B4..0x8751B8;
    temporary last-byte tests 0x8751DB/0x8751ED;
    trim repeats at 0x875223..0x875227;
    draw 0x875237.
  Equal speed path (native branch at 0x8755AF when value0 == value1):
    quotient production 0x8758D2..0x8758EB;
    dot 0x875966..0x875971;
    remainder production 0x875999..0x8759C2;
    first zero decision 0x875A07..0x875A18;
    second zero decision 0x875A21..0x875A32;
    remainder append 0x875A3B..0x875A4D;
    temporary trim length gate 0x875A56..0x875A5A;
    temporary last-byte tests 0x875A7B/0x875A8D;
    trim repeats at 0x875AC3..0x875AC7;
    return to shared draw 0x87585D..0x87586B.
  Unequal speed path:
    output = ratioComponent(value1) + "/" + ratioComponent(value0).
    ratioComponent(value):
      q = value / 1000;
      integerText = decimal(q); result = integerText;
      if integerText.length == 1:
        result += "." + decimal((value - 1000*q) / 100);
      return result.
    First quotient 0x8755CA..0x8755E3;
    first length gate 0x87565A..0x87565F;
    first fractional decimal at 0x875661..0x8756A7;
    separator "/" at 0x8756F8..0x875703;
    second quotient 0x875730..0x875749;
    second length gate 0x8757C0..0x8757C5;
    second fractional decimal at 0x8757C7..0x87580D;
    shared draw 0x87585D..0x87586B.
  Planar direction switches use (bits & 0xF) - 1 and allow ten table entries:
    climb switch 0x875314, table RVA 0x877114, default target 0x875343;
    speed switch 0x8758B7, table RVA 0x87713C, default target 0x875B0E.
    Valid planar outputs are ^, v, >, < and tile glyph bytes BF, DA, D9, C0;
    unsupported bit combinations follow the default with no planar glyph.
    Independent bit 0x10 adds glyph byte 0x18; bit 0x20 adds byte 0x19.
    Climb derives bits from coordinates; normal movement reads unit+0x4C4.
    These are direction indicators, not English wording to translate.
  native-switches.tsv preserves every entry, including compressed vegetation
  switch indices, their destinations and each default target for both images.

Visual stealth factors heading
  0x875CD2..0x875D02 -> "Visual Stealth Factors".

Lighting factor (0x875D11..0x8760DD)
  Read the unit tile at coordinates +0xA8/+0xAA/+0xAC.
  0x875D33 -> tile-object helper reference RVA 0x14A2970.
  0x875D3E -> null: continue map tile processing.
  0x875D45..0x875D5A -> object vfunc returns 9:
                       lightScore = 15, weatherScore = 25, "Low Light".
  0x875D5F..0x875E41 -> bounds/map block lookup;
                       tile designation flag at block+0x6A0 & 0x800000:
                       lightScore = 15, weatherScore = 25, "Low Light".
  0x875E69..0x875F1A -> invalid coordinates, missing map block, or absence of
                       block+0x2A0 & 0x4000:
                       lightScore = 3, weatherScore = 25, "Darkness".
  Else query weather helper 0x149DEF0 and light helper 0x149DE70.
  Weather result is capped at 25 at 0x875F3B..0x875F41.
  light >= 25 -> "Light" at 0x875FA5, draw 0x875FCA.
  3 < light < 25 -> "Low Light" at 0x87603D, draw 0x87605C.
  light <= 3 -> "Darkness" at 0x8760A4, draw 0x8760C6.

Weather factor (0x8760DD..0x8761CA)
  weather >= 25 -> "Clear" at 0x87610A, draw 0x87612F.
  weather < 25 -> "Fog/Rain/Snow" at 0x87614E, draw 0x876180.
  base stealth score = min(lightScore, weatherScore), at 0x8761C1..0x8761CA.

Obstacle factor (0x8761D1..0x8763EB)
  Query each in-bounds orthogonal neighbor using map helper 0x14A1530 with
  final argument 1 (four calls at 0x876202, 0x876243, 0x87627F, 0x8762C2).
  If any returns false -> score /= 2 (signed truncation toward zero),
                           "By Obstacle" at 0x87630E, draw 0x876342.
  Otherwise -> "Open Area" at 0x876381, draw 0x8763AA.

Vegetation factor (0x8763EB..0x87677E)
  body = int32(unit + 0x6B4).
  prone = uint32(unit + 0x110) & 0x8000.
  profile = prone ? body / 4 : body, at 0x8763FF..0x876409.
  0x8764E4 -> read unit tile type as uint16 map block tile array.
  capacity = 0 initially (native local initialized at 0x874987).
  tile type 0x22 or 0x185 -> capacity = 400 at 0x8764FC.
  Other tile types enter two indexed jump tables:
    table 1 values 0x31..0xE8, index RVA 0x87716C, destinations 0x877164;
    table 2 values 0x159..0x18D, index RVA 0x87722C, destinations 0x877224.
    grass/detail production target 0x876632 for:
      0x31..0x36, 0xE5..0xE8, 0x158..0x15B, 0x17F..0x182, 0x186..0x18D.
    all other values use capacity 0 at default target 0x876504.
  0x876632..0x876668 -> map grass/detail lookup with helpers
                       0x14D1330 and 0x14D850; missing -> capacity 0.
  0x8766A9 -> detail byte at tile's +0xC.
    detail >= 67 -> capacity = 400.
    33 < detail < 67 -> capacity = 200.
    detail <= 33 -> capacity = 0.
  profile < capacity -> score /= 2,
                        "In Vegetation" at 0x876550, draw 0x876582.
  otherwise:
    !prone and profile/4 < capacity ->
      "Non-Prone In Vegetation" at 0x876702, draw 0x876721.
    else capacity != 0 ->
      "Too Large For Vegetation" at 0x876731, draw 0x87674C.
    else -> "No Suitable Vegetation" at 0x876754, draw 0x87676F.
  These are separate native outcomes, not inferred from currently visible text.

Profile factor (0x87677E..0x876A9F)
  profile >= 500 -> score += profile / 100.
    !prone and profile < 2000:
      profile >= 1500 -> "Huge Non-Prone Profile" (0x8767E1/0x8767FC).
      profile >= 1000 -> "Very Large Non-Prone Profile" (0x87680F/0x87682A).
      else -> "Large Non-Prone Profile" (0x876835/0x876850).
    otherwise:
      profile >= 2500 -> "Gargantuan Profile" (0x876867/0x876882).
      profile >= 2000 -> "Gigantic Profile" (0x876895/0x8768B0).
      profile >= 1500 -> "Huge Profile" (0x8768C3/0x8768DE).
      profile >= 1000 -> "Very Large Profile" (0x8768F1/0x87690C).
      else -> "Large Profile" (0x876917/0x876932).
  profile < 200 -> score = (profile * score) / 200.
    profile == 0 -> "Vanishing Profile" (0x876970/0x87698B).
    profile < 50 -> "Minuscule Profile" (0x87699B/0x8769B6).
    profile < 100 -> "Tiny Profile" (0x8769C6/0x8769E1).
    profile < 150 -> "Very Small Profile" (0x8769F4/0x876A0F).
    else -> "Small Profile" (0x876A1A/0x876A35).
  200 <= profile < 500:
    !prone -> "Average Non-Prone Profile" (0x876A57/0x876A72).
    prone -> "Average Profile" (0x876A7A/0x876A95).

Visual stealth score (0x876AA4..0x876D7B)
  heading "Visual Stealth (w/o Skill)" at 0x876AE1, draw 0x876B15.
  score <= 0  -> "Best Possible" (0x876B5A/0x876B8C).
  score <= 2  -> "Fantastic" (0x876BE9/0x876C04).
  score <= 4  -> "Great" (0x876C1E/0x876C39).
  score <= 6  -> "Good" (0x876C53/0x876C6E).
  score <= 10 -> "Average" (0x876C88/0x876CA3).
  score <= 15 -> "Poor" (0x876CBD/0x876CD8).
  score <= 20 -> "Awful" (0x876CF2/0x876D0D).
  score <= 25 -> "Terrible" (0x876D24/0x876D3F).
  score > 25  -> "Worst Possible" (0x876D51/0x876D6C).
  Signed comparisons are used throughout this chain.
  explanation at 0x876DB7, draw 0x876DF4:
    "Quick movement and other actions decrease stealth."

Swimming preference (0x876E38..0x8770C4)
  shortcut enum 0x19F at 0x876E5E..0x876E63.
  heading " Swimming Preference" at 0x876E8A, draw 0x876EAF.
  Both option texts are always drawn, not selected by a text-producing branch.
  preference global: reference int16 RVA 0x2354B6C,
                     classic int16 RVA 0x234EA5C.
  value == 0 gives selected styling to first button (0x876EFC..0x876F39).
  value == 1 gives selected styling to second button (0x876FFC..0x87703B).
  first text "When possible" at 0x876F90, draw 0x876FC2.
  second text "When necessary" at 0x877087, draw 0x8770BA.

Shortcut production, all possible bindings
  shortcut() saves current draw color, uses the active keybinding display color,
  calls shortcut_name(active bindings, output, enum), draws it and restores color.
  shortcut_name() searches enum in the current binding map
    reference RVA 0x2390658 / classic RVA 0x238A548.
  If a binding exists and its list is nonempty, copy its first string at +0x20.
  Otherwise report "Missing binding displayed: " + enum-description and return
  the single visible character "?" (reference 0x8ECDF0).
  No alphabetic range restriction exists: remapped keys, multi-character names
  and modifier combinations are dynamic strings. The screenshot's a-f and s
  are examples of current bindings, not the full native text space.

Dynamic unit-title helper text paths
  Movement calls unit_title(unit, output, articleMode=1, capitalize=false,
                            final argument=true).
  unit-title functions have identical layouts, delta 0x5090.
  0x132E490..0x132E4CC: adventure mode + active adventurer -> you/You.
  0x132E4D6..0x132E4ED: unit+0xD80 object with nonempty string at +0x20
                         returns that string directly.
  0x132E4F2..0x132E4FE: global display mode 4/5 -> unit-name string +0x08.
  Named identity paths (0x132E52D..0x132ECFC and 0x132ED01..0x132F4F8):
    historical/identity object lookup from unit+0xC30/+0x1274;
    adventure relation/recognition conditions decide named display vs descriptor;
    race/caste/sex/type descriptor via helper reference 0x132E0C0;
    identity/group strings and title strings from named objects;
    status suffix " slave" or replacement "slave" from condition helper
      0xB973C0 and named object's +0xB4/+0xB8 fields;
    status suffix " prisoner" from condition helper 0xB98D90;
    use named output directly if descriptor absent, otherwise concatenate
      "the "/"The " + descriptor + " " + named output.
  Symbolic entity paths (0x132EEEC..0x132F025):
    entity object's flag byte at +0xC8 selects bit 0x4 -> "deity",
    bit 0x8 -> "force"; articleMode selects "the " vs "a " vs none.
  Species/descriptor fallback (0x132F4FE..0x132F8DF):
    0x132F51A..0x132F53B, if species helper true, unit+0x3BC == -1 and
      unit+0x110 & 0x4000000, select "stray " or "fierce " according to
      civilization object flag at object+0x3A0, byte +7 & 0x10.
    else unit+0x11C & 0x1000 -> "agitated ".
    unit+0x118 & 0x1000 -> "ghost" or "ghostly " depending on an empty
      descriptor/name decision.
    if output is still empty, articleMode 1 -> "the ", 0 -> "a ", else none.
    adventure mode -> body descriptor from unit+0x13E8, except "average"
      (0x132F74B..0x132F762 explicitly suppresses that neutral descriptor).
    unit+0x838 and nonempty unit+0x880 with empty unit+0x840 -> prepend
      the +0x880 name and a space.
    append the generated raw race/caste descriptor string.
    unit+0x838 with nonempty unit+0x840 -> append that dynamic string.
    unit+0xD80 nonnull -> append "corpse" or " corpse".
    capitalization is optional and disabled for this modal's helper call.
  Exact predicates, raw source operands and all named-helper calls are preserved
  in both unit-title ASM files and the native TSV inventories.

Native drawing/storage artifacts
  Frame edges, selected row/button tint, scrollbar behavior, SSO/heap allocation,
  string buffer cleanup and error-handler branches are included in full ASM and
  native-branches.tsv. They do not produce additional UI wording.
  Disassembly after each function's ret includes jump-table data; invalid decoded
  opcodes in that area are table bytes, not omitted executable text branches.
